title: Ecological fallacy: positive district correlation vs negative within-district slope
what: District means correlate positively (r = +1.00), but within every district student slope is negative (mean r = -0.77)

reader_questions.question: How does the within-district correlation compare to the district-aggregate correlation?
reader_questions.expected: Aggregate r is +1.00, but within every district student-level correlation reverses to r ≈ -0.77.

reader_questions.question: Why does the sign flip between district and student levels?
reader_questions.expected: Affluent districts have both higher baseline scores and more tutoring, while struggling students within each district take more tutoring.

reader_questions.question: Why would plotting only 5 district averages mislead policy?
reader_questions.expected: It commits the ecological fallacy, inferring an individual-level positive effect from a group-level correlation.
